controller.title: Who is responsible
controller.text: The data controller is José Manuel Pérez Monge (IGO Tech project). Contact: igotech@gmail.com.

data.title: What we collect
data.text: The details you enter in the early access form: your name, email address and product interest, and optionally your company, role and a message.

purpose.title: Why we use it
purpose.text: To reply to your request and to contact you about early access to IGO. We do not use your details for anything else.

basis.title: Legal basis
basis.text: Your consent, which you give by ticking the box in the form. You can withdraw it at any time.

recipients.title: Who receives it
recipients.text: A form-processing service provider receives each request on our behalf and forwards it to us by email. We do not sell your details.

retention.title: How long we keep it
retention.text: Only as long as needed to handle your request and early access communications, or until you ask us to delete it.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.text: You can ask us to access, correct or delete your details, to restrict or object to their use, or to withdraw your consent, by contacting the controller above. You can also complain to your data protection authority.

hero.title: IGO Research
hero.intro: A space to understand the technology we carry with us: how it works, what information it provides and which questions to ask before trusting its results.
hero.note: Educational content and analysis of public sources on technology and human experience.
hero.imageAlt: Conceptual composition of glasses and a technology ring

technology.title: Understand what lies behind each feature.
technology.wearables: A device can record signals and turn them into indicators. To interpret them, it helps to distinguish what the sensor detects from what the software calculates.
technology.glasses: Audio, cameras and displays are different features. The word “smart” does not tell you which ones a model includes or how its services work.
technology.ai: A useful answer starts with suitable data and a well-framed question. Clarity does not prove correctness.
technology.sensorAlt: Conceptual view of the optical sensors inside a ring

chain.title: From a signal to an interpretation.
chain.signal: A sensor records a physical change.
chain.quality: The system checks whether the signal is usable.
chain.read: The result is read alongside operating conditions and limitations.
chain.feedback: If quality is insufficient, check placement or repeat the reading according to the manual. Repetition alone does not turn an estimate into a validated measurement.
chain.caption: Conceptual diagram: the actual process depends on the device.

human.title: The person is part of the system.
human.text: Sleep, attention and the way we interact with an interface help us ask better questions about technology. This space considers both the data and the experience of the person using it.

limits.title: Measuring, estimating and interpreting are different things.
limits.text: Before accepting a conclusion, we ask what was recorded, how the result was produced and under which conditions it was evaluated. A commercial specification describes a feature; it does not replace a performance evaluation.

picks.title: Ideas for a better understanding of technology.
picks.text: Short guides connecting mechanisms, uses and limitations.

igo.title: Understand before you choose.
igo.text: IGO Research brings together explanations to help you ask better questions when reading a specification: what the device records, what depends on a phone or connection, and what evidence supports each feature. Product capabilities must be checked against the documentation for that model.
